notes:
There are now three plans instead of six: Solo, Studio and Agency. If you are on one of the older plans nothing changes — it still works and you keep everything you had. Three features that existed in the app but belonged to no plan start at Studio: uploading to social media, sports mode, and subtitle translation.

A scheduled upload now holds even when your computer is off. The video is sent to YouTube half an hour ahead of time and YouTube publishes it at the minute you picked, so it shows as Scheduled in your Studio whether or not the app is running. Once it goes up the clip moves to Published instead of sitting in Approved, and the row shows the result with a link to the video. Cancelling is honest about what it can do: the row goes away, but a video already uploaded stays on YouTube, because the app is not allowed to delete videos.

The review queue is a triage screen again. It has three buttons — Approve, Trim and Reject — and the polish tools have moved to the Clips page, where the clip you approved is the clip you actually work on: subtitles, images and text live there now. Trim stays in review because it is the one tool that changes the keep-or-drop decision. With fewer buttons per row they are twice as wide and the labels read properly.

Framing is more careful. A face inside the game no longer counts as a camera and gets pushed into the top band — the app measures how much of the frame it fills, looks for agreement across frames, and falls back to full-frame when it cannot be sure. Whether a broadcast is a full match or a highlight reel is decided by its length rather than by the audio, so opening music is no longer mistaken for a moment worth clipping. The scoreboard is measured from the video instead of assumed to sit in a fixed rectangle, so channels that place it differently still work.

Scheduled uploads show a real percentage while they run. When YouTube refuses an upload you get a sentence explaining why instead of a wall of raw text. The clip picker has a delete button, which moves the clip to Rejected rather than erasing it.
